overview:
Arizona's 7th District leans firmly Democratic, and incumbent Adelita Grijalva is running for re-election after being renominated. She has raised about $2.6 million and holds roughly $438,000 on hand, while Republican Daniel Butierez has raised about $234,000 with just over $11,000 available. Outside groups have spent modestly to support her and little against her, and no outside spending is recorded on behalf of the Republican challenger.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the wide money gap. Prediction markets on Polymarket price the Democratic nominee around 96 percent to win. Every available indicator points to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin, with the seat rated safe for the party that holds it.
